verses.text: After this, the people of Moab and Ammon, together with some of the Meunites, came to fight against Jehoshaphat.
Some men came and told Jehoshaphat, "A huge army is coming against you from Edom, from the other side of the Dead Sea. Look, they are already at Hazazon Tamar," which is En Gedi.
Jehoshaphat was afraid, and he decided to ask the LORD for help. He announced that everyone in Judah should go without food.
The people of Judah came together to ask the LORD for help. They came from every town in Judah to seek the LORD.
Jehoshaphat stood up in front of the people of Judah and Jerusalem at the LORD's temple, in front of the new courtyard.
He said, "LORD, God of our ancestors, aren't you the God in heaven? You rule over all the kingdoms of the nations. You have power and strength, and no one can stand against you.
Our God, didn't you drive out the people who lived in this land ahead of your people Israel? Didn't you give it forever to the descendants of your friend Abraham?
They have lived in it and built a temple here to honor your name. They said,

'If trouble comes on us, whether war, punishment, disease, or famine, we will stand in front of this temple and in front of you, because your name is in this temple. We will cry out to you in our trouble, and you will hear us and save us.'
Now look at the people of Ammon, Moab, and Mount Seir. When Israel came out of Egypt, you did not let them invade these nations. So Israel turned away from them and did not destroy them.
Now look how they repay us! They are coming to drive us out of the land you gave us as our own.
Our God, won't you judge them? We have no power against this huge army that is attacking us. We do not know what to do, but our eyes are on you."
All the men of Judah stood there in front of the LORD, with their babies, their wives, and their children.
Then the LORD's Spirit came on Jahaziel, there in the middle of the crowd. He was a Levite from the family of Asaph, the son of Zechariah, son of Benaiah, son of Jeiel, son of Mattaniah.
He said, "Listen, all Judah, people of Jerusalem, and King Jehoshaphat! The LORD says to you: 'Do not be afraid or discouraged because of this huge army. The battle is not yours, but God's.
Tomorrow, go down to meet them. They will be coming up the pass of Ziz. You will find them at the end of the valley, facing the desert of Jeruel.

You will not need to fight this battle. Take your places, stand still, and watch the LORD save you, Judah and Jerusalem. Do not be afraid or discouraged. Go out to face them tomorrow, because the LORD is with you.'"
Jehoshaphat bowed down with his face to the ground. All the people of Judah and Jerusalem fell down in front of the LORD and worshiped him.
Then some Levites from the families of Kohath and Korah stood up and praised the LORD, the God of Israel, with a very loud voice.

Early the next morning they went out into the desert of Tekoa. As they set out, Jehoshaphat stood and said, "Listen to me, Judah and people of Jerusalem! Believe in the LORD your God, and you will stand firm. Believe his prophets, and you will succeed."
After talking with the people, he chose singers to go ahead of the army, praising the LORD for his holy beauty. They sang, "Give thanks to the LORD, because his love lasts forever."
As soon as they began to sing and praise, the LORD set ambushes against the people of Ammon, Moab, and Mount Seir who were attacking Judah, and they were defeated.
The armies of Ammon and Moab turned against the people of Mount Seir and destroyed them completely. When they had finished off the people of Seir, they turned and destroyed each other.
When the men of Judah came to the place that looks out over the desert, they looked toward the huge army. All they saw were dead bodies lying on the ground. No one had escaped.

Jehoshaphat and his people came to collect the loot. Among the bodies they found lots of goods, clothes, and valuable things. They took more than they could carry. There was so much that it took them three days to collect it all.
On the fourth day they gathered in the Valley of Beracah, where they praised the LORD. That is why it is still called the Valley of Beracah, which means Valley of Praise, to this day.
Then all the men of Judah and Jerusalem, with Jehoshaphat leading them, went back to Jerusalem full of joy, because the LORD had given them joy over their enemies.
They came into Jerusalem and went to the LORD's temple with harps, lyres, and trumpets.
The fear of God fell on all the kingdoms of those lands when they heard how the LORD had fought against Israel's enemies.
So Jehoshaphat's kingdom was at peace, because his God gave him rest on every side.
So Jehoshaphat ruled over Judah. He was thirty-five years old when he became king, and he ruled for twenty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother was Azubah, daughter of Shilhi.
He followed the ways of his father Asa and did not turn away from them. He did what was right in the LORD's eyes.
But the hilltop shrines were not removed, and the people still had not set their hearts on the God of their ancestors.
Everything else Jehoshaphat did, from beginning to end, is written in the records of Jehu son of Hanani, which are part of the book of the kings of Israel.
Later, Jehoshaphat king of Judah made an agreement with Ahaziah king of Israel, who was very wicked.
They agreed to build ships to sail to Tarshish. They built the ships at Ezion Geber.

Then Eliezer son of Dodavahu from Mareshah prophesied against Jehoshaphat. He said, "Because you joined with Ahaziah, the LORD will destroy what you have made." The ships were wrecked and could not sail to Tarshish.
